screening_decisions.reason: This RCT compares patient decision aids (DAs), not PROMs feedback. While surgeons receive patient preference reports, these are not patient-reported outcome measures being fed back to inform care. The intervention focuses on decision-making aids rather than PROMs feedback to healthcare providers or patients.

This RCT tests whether informing dentists about patients' dental anxiety scores (from MDAS questionnaire) reduces patient anxiety. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare providers (dentists) compared to no feedback, assessing effects on patient-reported outcomes (state anxiety).

This RCT compares session-by-session progress feedback using the Outcome Rating Scale (a PROM) to therapists vs no feedback. It directly assesses effects of PROMs feedback to healthcare providers on therapeutic outcomes.

This RCT compares PROMs feedback to therapist+supervisor vs therapist only. While both arms receive some feedback, the intervention adds supervision feedback. This could be relevant for understanding how PROMs feedback delivery affects outcomes, though the control arm does receive feedback.

This RCT tests an eHealth app that monitors HRQOL and symptoms with tailored feedback to patients vs delayed access. This is PROMs feedback to patients, assessing effects on patient activation and self-management outcomes.
This is a literature review, not a randomised trial. It reviews existing evidence about PRO graphical displays but does not test PROMs feedback effects.

This RCT includes self-monitoring with graphical and nurse-initiated feedback of patient-reported data vs standard care. The intervention includes PROMs feedback components (quality of life, depression, anxiety data) to healthcare providers.

This RCT compares HRQL assessment with feedback to physicians vs no feedback vs no measurement. It directly tests PROMs feedback to healthcare providers on patient outcomes and processes of care (communication).

This RCT tests whether informing physicians of depression screening results (Zung Self-Rating Depression Scale) vs not informing affects diagnosis and treatment. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare providers.

This is a laboratory study about DUI offenders and driving ability feedback, not a clinical trial of PROMs feedback in healthcare. The context and population are outside the scope of clinical PROMs feedback.
This RCT tests whether reporting anxiety symptom levels and functioning status to primary care physicians vs not reporting affects patient outcomes. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare providers.
This is a validation study of the SF-36 questionnaire, not a randomised trial comparing PROMs feedback vs no feedback. It assesses psychometric properties without testing feedback effects.

This RCT includes Featback, an automated monitoring and feedback system for ED symptoms. While it's an economic evaluation, the underlying trial tests PROMs feedback (with varying therapist support) vs waiting list.

This RCT compares physicians receiving reports of patients' physical, psychological, and social function vs no reports. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare providers assessing effects on patient function.

This RCT includes symptom monitoring with feedback vs no feedback conditions. The intervention involves PROMs (symptom monitoring) feedback to patients, assessing effects on trigger identification and quality of life.

This is a feasibility RCT for a supportive care intervention. The abstract is limited, but supportive care interventions often include PROMs assessment and feedback. Including conservatively pending full text review.
This is a structured review, not a randomised trial. While it reviews PROMs evidence, it does not test PROMs feedback effects directly.
Despite the title, this is an observational study about VTE risk in immune-mediated diseases using hospital records. It does not involve PROMs feedback or randomised comparison.

This RCT tests whether systematic pain assessment information (pain battery and depression scale) sent to physicians vs usual care affects clinical practices and patient outcomes. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare providers.
Despite the title mentioning PROMs, the abstract describes a tool validation study for self-care activities during COVID-19 lockdown. This is not a randomised trial testing PROMs feedback effects.
This RCT tests whether using the Work Stress Questionnaire with physicians' feedback vs treatment as usual affects healthcare visits and treatment. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare providers.

This RCT compares monthly telephone monitoring of distress (using HADS and EORTC questionnaires) with referral vs educational materials alone. This includes PROMs monitoring with feedback leading to referrals.
This RCT compares OQ-45.2 feedback system vs no feedback for psychotherapy patients. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare providers assessing effects on therapy outcomes.
This pilot RCT tests a mobile app with weekly symptom reporting (ESAS) and recommendations vs control. This includes PROMs monitoring with feedback to patients about supportive care services.
This is a cross-sectional mixed-methods study about PRO data presentation formats, not a randomised trial testing PROMs feedback effects on outcomes or processes of care.
This RCT tests knowledge test feedback vs routine education, not PROMs feedback. The feedback is about knowledge/surgical information, not patient-reported outcomes.
This is a qualitative interview study with GPs about their opinions on depression severity questionnaires, not a randomised trial testing PROMs feedback effects.

This is a feasibility cluster-RCT of a self-management programme. While the abstract focuses on self-efficacy, such programmes often include PROMs assessment. Including conservatively pending full text review.

This RCT tests whether telling patients and/or physicians PRIME-MD screening results vs not telling affects psychiatric consultation/referral. This is PROMs feedback to both patients and healthcare providers.

This is a protocol/design paper for a cluster-RCT testing automated interactive voice response providing physicians with real-time patient-reported data vs educational calls. The study design fits the criteria, though results are not yet available.
This RCT compares HRQL assessment with interpretive assistance (feedback) vs HRQL assessment only vs usual care. This tests PROMs feedback to healthcare providers on patient outcomes.

This RCT tests making patient-reported cancer needs, QOL, and psychosocial information available to healthcare team vs not. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare providers with coordinated interventions.

This is a protocol for a pragmatic RCT testing self-monitoring with personalized feedback vs no additional intervention for depression. The design fits the criteria (PROMs feedback), though results are not yet available.

This RCT compares an automated self-monitoring and feedback intervention (Featback) with different levels of therapist support against a waiting list control. The primary comparison is intervention vs waiting list, not PROMs feedback vs no PROMs feedback. The feedback is to patients themselves as part of a therapeutic intervention rather than PROMs feedback to healthcare providers for clinical decision-making.
This is a scoping review, not a randomized trial. The abstract explicitly states 'We conducted a scoping review on quality of care and multimorbidity'.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing PROMs feedback (to telephone caseworkers or oncologists/GPs) vs usual care (no feedback). Patient-reported outcomes include anxiety, depression, physical/emotional functioning, and unmet supportive care needs. Meets all inclusion criteria.
This is a methodological paper about meta-analysis techniques, not a randomized trial. The abstract is truncated but clearly describes Cochrane Review methodology.

This RCT compares QoL questionnaire with feedback (intervention group) vs questionnaire without feedback (attention group) vs no questionnaire (control). Outcomes include QoL issues identified, actions taken, and global QoL. Meets inclusion criteria.

This randomized trial compares feedback of depression screening results (Zung scale) to physicians vs no feedback. Outcomes include physician notations about depression and treatment (process of care). Meets inclusion criteria.
This is a qualitative interview study with 60 oncologists, not a randomized trial. No intervention comparison is made.
This is a meta-analysis and theory paper, not a randomized trial. It reviews 607 effect sizes from various studies.

This RCT compares computer-generated health status reports (AIMS or MHAQ scores) vs control. Outcomes include medication compliance, physician visits, referrals, and health status. Meets inclusion criteria.
This RCT compares summary of pain scales provided to oncologists vs no summary. Outcomes include prescription patterns and pain incidence. Meets inclusion criteria.
This is a tool development study, not a randomized trial. It describes creating and validating a new assessment tool (EMPRO).
This cluster-randomized trial compares tobacco cessation counseling vs usual care, not PROMs feedback. The intervention is counseling, not feedback of patient-reported outcome measures.
This is a theory-driven review paper, not a randomized trial. It summarizes evidence from other RCTs rather than conducting a primary trial.
This RCT compares daily electronic symptom reporting (PRO-CTCAE) with feedback to nurses vs control. Outcomes include symptom burden. Meets inclusion criteria.
This RCT compares symptom monitoring with automated alerts to clinicians vs no alerts. Outcomes include symptom threshold events and symptom interference. Meets inclusion criteria.
This randomized trial compares feedback of GHQ screening information to clinicians vs no feedback. Outcomes include detection of mental health problems and management. Meets inclusion criteria.

This RCT includes a patient self-assessment arm where patients calculate Disease Activity Score reported to rheumatologist vs control. Outcomes include DMARD therapy changes and comorbidity measures. Meets inclusion criteria.
This RCT compares OQ-45 with feedback vs control group. Outcomes include OQ-45 total score and alertness for treatment failure. Meets inclusion criteria.
This RCT compares web-mediated follow-up with self-scored symptoms and alerts to oncologist vs routine follow-up. Outcomes include overall survival and performance status. Meets inclusion criteria.
This is a tool development and validation study, not a randomized trial. It describes creating the NFI-MND scale.
This RCT compares feedback of personality test results vs assessment-only (no feedback). Outcomes include treatment engagement, length of stay, and relationships. Meets inclusion criteria.
This is a review/opinion paper, not a randomized trial. It discusses the use of PROs in healthcare but does not conduct a trial.
This RCT compares HRQL questionnaire with graphic summary to physicians and patients vs control. Outcomes include communication and physician awareness. Meets inclusion criteria.
This RCT compares PROMIS symptom scores provided to clinicians vs no scores. Outcomes include symptom scores, documentation, and clinician actions. Meets inclusion criteria.
This RCT compares QoL assessment with feedback to clinicians vs standard assessment alone. Outcomes include patient satisfaction and clinical outcomes. Meets inclusion criteria.
This RCT compares PRO feedback (PediQUEST) to oncologists and families vs no feedback. Outcomes include symptom distress and HRQoL. Meets inclusion criteria.
This RCT compares evidence-based screening tools (PEDS, M-CHAT, PHQ9) with feedback vs usual care. Outcomes include detection rates and referral rates. Meets inclusion criteria.
This RCT compares QoL profile and expert report to practitioner vs standard care. Outcomes include diseased QoL rates. Meets inclusion criteria.
This is a cluster-randomized trial comparing quality monitoring with feedback (TK-Modell) vs traditional procedure. Outcomes include treatment outcomes and costs. Meets inclusion criteria.
This RCT compares elcss-ql data provided to oncologist vs standard assessment alone. Outcomes include PC referral rates and hrqol scores. Meets inclusion criteria.
This randomized controlled study compares GHQ scores provided to physicians vs no scores. Outcomes include psychiatric diagnosis and psychosocial referral. Meets inclusion criteria.
This RCT compares disclosure of depression scores to GPs vs no disclosure. Outcomes include depression scores at 6 and 12 months. Meets inclusion criteria.
This RCT compares ESRA-C graphical summary to clinical team vs no summary. Outcomes include discussion of SQLIs. Meets inclusion criteria.

RCT but the FLARE-RA questionnaire is used to trigger interventions (nurse counseling/expedited visits) rather than provide PROMs feedback to providers/patients about outcomes. The focus is on flare management intervention, not PROMs feedback effects.
Not a randomized trial - appears to be a descriptive article about PROMs use in practice.
Not a randomized trial - this is a review/framework paper about implementing PROs.
RCT but the intervention is life review therapy, not PROMs feedback. No PROMs feedback component to healthcare providers or patients.
RCT about depression screening program. While WHOQOL-Bref is used as outcome measure, the intervention is about communicating screening results and offering treatment, not PROMs feedback per se.
Practice-randomized trial about depression care management program. Not specifically about PROMs feedback - focuses on algorithm-based care management.

RCT comparing AEP (Adverse Event Profile) scores made available to physicians vs not. AEP is a PROM measuring adverse effects, and feedback is provided to healthcare providers. Directly compares effects of PROMs feedback on outcomes.

RCT comparing PCOMS (Partners for Change Outcome Management System) feedback to therapists vs treatment as usual. PCOMS is a PROM feedback system that monitors patient outcomes and provides feedback to therapists.
Cluster RCT but the monitoring tool tracks physical activity (behavioral monitoring), not patient-reported outcome measures. Physical activity tracking is not typically considered PROMs feedback.

RCT with PCSQ feedback but conducted in experimental setting with undergraduates, not clinical practice. While it examines feedback effects, it's not testing PROMs feedback in healthcare clinical practice.
Cluster RCT but focuses on youth violence screening (risk behavior), not PROMs. The electronic PVQ assesses risk behaviors rather than patient-reported health outcomes.
RCT using QoL-monitor assessing QoL, distress and care needs with feedback to both HCPs and patients. Directly compares PROMs feedback effects on communication and outcomes.

RCT where screening questionnaire (SQ) results including scales for anxiety, depression, somatisation were disclosed to GPs vs blinded. Directly compares effects of PROMs feedback on GP recognition and care provision.
Not a randomized trial - this is a methodological paper developing a classification system for PRO measures.
Cluster RCT providing physicians with alcohol screening results (CAGE questionnaire) and recommendations. Directly compares PROMs feedback effects on physician discussions and patient outcomes.
Not a primary randomized trial - appears to be a systematic review protocol about PROMs in mental health care.
RCT but focuses on sun protection behavior feedback, not PROMs feedback. The abstract is truncated but appears to be about behavioral intervention.
Cluster RCT but the intervention is a communication tool (Loop), not specifically PROMs feedback. While patient-reported measures are collected, the focus is on team communication.
Cluster RCT providing surgeons with peer benchmarked PROMs feedback (OHS, HOOS, EQ-5D). Directly compares effects of PROMs feedback on patient outcomes.
RCT comparing feedback about patient progress to therapists vs control. Uses outcome monitoring with feedback to therapists, directly comparing PROMs feedback effects on treatment outcomes.
RCT providing GPs with results of computerized assessment (GHQ, PROQSY) of common mental disorders. Directly compares PROMs feedback effects on clinical outcomes.
RCT using KIDSCREEN-27 (HRQOL PROM) with face-to-face discussion of results with physicians. Directly compares PROMs feedback effects on HRQOL outcomes.
Cluster RCT but focuses on risk-stratification strategy (STarT Back) implementation, not specifically PROMs feedback. The tool is used for stratification, not primarily for feedback provision.
RCT but the intervention is a recovery-focused psychiatric package with written feedback, not specifically PROMs feedback. Focus is on recovery-oriented care, not PROMs feedback effects.
Not a randomized trial - this is a guidance document from the Medical Research Council.

RCT comparing computer-generated feedback letters (based on alcohol screening) vs assessment only. The feedback letters constitute PROMs feedback to patients, directly comparing feedback effects on outcomes.
RCT protocol but focuses on acceptability of PROM administration methods, not on effects of PROMs feedback on outcomes or processes of care.
RCT providing SF-36 results to physicians before patient encounters. Directly compares PROMs feedback effects on process of care and patient outcomes.
RCT but focuses on health risk behavior screening (not PROMs) with feedback. Risk behaviors are not patient-reported outcome measures of health status.
Not a randomized trial - this is a realist synthesis review about PROMs use in clinical care.
RCT where patients report symptoms and preferences via computer, provided to clinicians before consultation. Directly compares patient-reported outcome feedback effects on care processes.
RCT comparing AEP (Adverse Events Profile) scores provided to clinicians vs usual care. AEP is a PROM for adverse effects, directly comparing PROMs feedback effects on outcomes.

RCT comparing standard care vs MTH intervention that includes self-monitoring, data transmission, and graphical/nurse-initiated feedback. Involves patient-reported data with feedback to nurses. Outcomes include self-efficacy, illness beliefs, and self-care.

RCT with 3 groups (treatment as usual, therapist feedback, patient-therapist feedback) examining effects of providing treatment progress information. Uses patient-focused research systems to monitor and inform therapists.
Questionnaire development and psychometric testing study, not a randomised trial. No intervention comparing PROMs feedback vs no feedback.
Cluster RCT where oncologists were randomized to receive immediate print-out of patient-reported symptoms (LoMoS) or not. Uses Edmonton-Symptom-Assessment-Scale and other patient-reported measures.
Group RCT with clinicians randomized to usual care or CDS using symptom assessment. Patients completed web-based symptom assessments, clinicians received tailored reports with management suggestions.
RCT evaluating real-time daily patient feedback to providers using patient experience surveys (HCAHPS) with feedback to physicians along with provider coaching.
Observational study examining physician-patient agreement about depression and medical record notation. Not a randomised trial.
Cochrane review protocol/overview, not a primary randomised trial. Does not meet study design criteria.
RCT evaluating detailed feedback about a patient's mental health problem and desires for specific mental health interventions. Compared control, feedback, and feedback/protocol groups.
RCT comparing symptom monitoring plus feedback vs usual care. Uses HRQOL and symptom assessments (PROMs) with feedback to providers.

RCT with computer-generated feedback to physicians about patient's functional status using the Functional Status Questionnaire. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs no feedback.

RCT with 3 conditions (feedback to therapist, feedback to therapist and patient, no feedback) using the Outcome Questionnaire. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals and/or patients vs no feedback.

RCT with intervention group completing monthly postal questionnaires assessing needs, quality of life, mental health problem severity, and receiving 3-monthly feedback. Directly compares PROMs feedback vs treatment as usual.

RCT comparing CBT guided self-care with vs without personalized feedback on current physical and psychological status. Feedback to patients delivered via personalized letters, feedback forms, and computerised feedback.

RCT investigating the effect of systematic symptom monitoring using the Symptom Monitor on symptom prevalence and severity in palliative cancer patients. Directly compares PROMs monitoring/feedback vs no monitoring.

RCT where patients reported 12 common symptoms via tablet computers, with physicians receiving symptom printouts and nurses receiving email alerts for severe symptoms. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs usual care.

RCT with patients randomly assigned to feedback or no-feedback control condition. Uses outcome monitoring with feedback to therapists. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs no feedback.
RCT comparing a video decision aid to standard educational materials on lung cancer screening decisions. This is about decision aids, not PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals or patients.
RCT with screening and nursing assessment intervention for older ED patients. Uses ISAR screening tool but this is about screening and referral, not PROMs feedback to providers/patients.

RCT where patients reported AEs weekly by an electronic PRO-tool based on PRO-CTCAE platform, compared to standard monitoring alone. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs standard monitoring.

RCT where patients self-reported symptoms daily, with intervention group having symptom reports presented graphically with alerts during daily team rounds. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs usual care.
RCT comparing smartphone apps for symptom/biomarker monitoring vs standard face-to-face care. Focus is on noninferiority of care delivery method rather than PROMs feedback effects.

RCT giving patients access to Sanoia platform for self-assessment vs usual care. While it involves patient self-monitoring, it is unclear if there is feedback to providers. Focus is on patient-physician interactions rather than PROMs feedback effects.

RCT testing ecological momentary intervention with SMS-based feedback on alcohol consumption. This is about alcohol use intervention, not PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals or patients for health outcomes.

Cluster RCT where patients provided information on treatment outcome via weekly computerised standardised assessments, with patients and clinicians in intervention group receiving continuous feedback. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals and patients vs no feedback.

RCT examining physician clinical decision making with intervention physicians provided HAM-D scores and treatment recommendations. This is about physician decision making and treatment algorithms, not specifically PROMs feedback effects.

Feasibility RCT with web-based app for real-time symptom monitoring. Patients self-reported health information integrated into electronic health records, with alerts triggered for medical intervention. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs no feedback.

Pilot study with automated telephone-based IVR intervention where patients rated pain and symptoms, with oncologists receiving email alerts for moderate to severe symptoms. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs no feedback.
Questionnaire development and psychometric testing study, not a randomised trial. No intervention comparing PROMs feedback vs no feedback.

Cluster RCT with two feedback strategies (generic and individual patient-specific End-of-Life in Dementia scores) compared to no feedback. Uses PROMs completed by family caregivers with feedback to nursing home staff.
Descriptive article summarizing the organization and scientific activity of the PROMIS network. Not a randomised trial.
RCT comparing hospital-based follow-up vs nurse-led telephone follow-up for endometrial cancer patients. This is about follow-up method, not PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals or patients.
RCT comparing physician-targeted interventions with patient-specific treatment recommendations based on depression screening (CES-D, HAM-D) vs usual care. This involves PROMs feedback to physicians.
RCT in oncology comparing ITPA assessment summaries provided to physicians/nurses vs no summary. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare providers comparing outcomes.
RCT with three arms comparing ESM self-monitoring with/without feedback sessions vs treatment as usual. Involves PROMs feedback to patients.
RCT comparing Nintendo Wii virtual rehabilitation vs conventional physical therapy. Not about PROMs feedback - compares two treatment modalities.
RCT comparing treatment progress and alliance feedback to clients and therapists vs treatment as usual in couple therapy. This is PROMs feedback.
Validation study of Dartmouth COOP Charts reliability and validity. Not an RCT comparing feedback vs no feedback.
RCT comparing PROMIS Pain Interference CAT feedback to patients vs no feedback in orthopedic surgery. Directly tests PROMs feedback effects.
RCT comparing feedback regarding client progress plus clinical support tools vs treatment as usual in psychotherapy. This is PROMs feedback.
Systematic review of literature, not a primary RCT. Does not meet inclusion criteria for primary studies.
RCT with general practices as intervention units comparing feedback of patient asthma information to primary care teams vs no feedback. This is PROMs feedback.
Opinion/policy paper about NHS Outcomes Framework. Not a primary RCT.
RCT comparing PRIME-MD psychiatric interview results given to physicians vs no-report in ED. This is PROMs feedback to clinicians.
RCT with stratified random assignment comparing SIP functional assessment instrument use vs control. Involves PROMs feedback to physicians.
RCT comparing Dartmouth COOP Charts health status assessment vs no measure in HMO. This is PROMs feedback to clinicians.
RCT comparing standard mHealth vs mHealth with automated feedback to informal caregivers about patient status. Involves PROMs feedback.
RCT comparing stellate ganglion block vs sham for PTSD. Not about PROMs feedback - compares treatment vs sham procedure.
RCT comparing PROMs monitoring for depression with feedback vs control in primary care. Directly tests PROMs feedback effects.
RCT comparing clinicians receiving clinical feedback reports from patient-reported mental health assessments vs no report. This is PROMs feedback.
Cluster RCT comparing DIALOG intervention (patients rate quality of life/treatment with feedback to clinicians) vs TAU. This is PROMs feedback.
Observational study of HRQoL in overweight youth. Not an RCT comparing PROMs feedback vs control.
RCT comparing feedback of General Health Questionnaire screening results to clinicians vs no feedback in primary care. This is PROMs feedback.
RCT comparing patient/therapist feedback plus clinical decision-support tools vs treatment as usual. This is PROMs feedback.
RCT comparing depression self-rating scale with person-centred discussion vs TAU in primary care. This is PROMs feedback.
Systematic review of controlled trials, not a primary RCT. Does not meet inclusion criteria for primary studies.
RCT comparing physical function assessments with feedback to patient and physician vs functional assessments alone. This is PROMs feedback.
Review paper summarizing ISOQOL User's Guide for implementing PROs. Not a primary RCT.
Qualitative study using interviews and focus groups. Not an RCT.
Study protocol for a planned RCT. No results available - protocol only.
Bibliographic study of quality of life measures. Not a primary RCT.
RCT comparing eSAID questionnaire with report to dentist vs control version in children. This is PROMs feedback to clinicians.
RCT comparing monitoring and discussing psychological well-being with Well-being Questionnaire vs standard care in diabetes. This is PROMs feedback.
Opinion/educational paper about PRO implementation barriers. Not a primary RCT.

RCT but focuses on tailored feedback messages for health behavior change, not PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals. The feedback is behavioral/self-efficacy focused, not patient-reported outcome measures used in clinical practice.
Qualitative study with 6 health visitor interviews, not a randomised trial. Does not meet study design criteria.
RCT comparing PHQ-9 screening with feedback to providers (intervention) vs control. PHQ-9 is a PROM measuring depression symptoms. Study examines effects on patient outcomes and physician management.
Validation study of hearing loss screening tool (HSAQ) against audiometric evaluation. Not a randomised trial comparing PROMs feedback vs no feedback.
Study about physiology feedback (heart rate monitoring) on self-reported stress in lab setting. Not PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals in clinical practice.

Cluster RCT using Readiness for Hospital Discharge Scale (PROM) with patient self-assessment component. Compares PROMs-based discharge readiness assessment with usual care. Examines effects on readmissions and processes of care.
RCT but clinicians received summaries of participant reports in BOTH groups (intervention and control). No comparison of PROMs feedback vs no feedback - both received feedback.

Study about depression screening questionnaire feedback to residents. Appears to compare screening feedback vs no feedback on recognition of depression. Limited abstract detail but likely meets criteria.
RCT comparing OQ-45 (PROM) feedback to therapists vs treatment-as-usual without feedback. Examines effects on patient outcomes for at-risk patients. Clear comparison of PROMs feedback vs no feedback.
Literature review, not a primary randomised trial. Does not meet study design criteria.
Study about syndromic surveillance app for disease detection, not PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals in clinical practice. Different purpose and context.

RCT comparing HRQL (HUI2, HUI3) completion with feedback to clinicians (graphical representation in chart) vs without feedback. Clear comparison of PROMs feedback vs no feedback on communication, management, and outcomes.
RCT but intervention is web-based self-management portal with nurse case manager support. Not specifically comparing PROMs feedback to clinicians vs no feedback.
RCT comparing different levels of distress screening (PROMs) with varying feedback and triage options. Compares minimal screening vs full screening vs triage. Examines effects on distress outcomes.
Methodological debate paper about systematic reviews, not a primary randomised trial.
RCT about communication skills training for oncologists, not about PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.

Cluster RCT comparing GDS (PROM) screening with physician notification vs no notification. Clear comparison of PROMs feedback to clinicians vs no feedback. Examines diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes.
RCT comparing BDI (PROM) score disclosure to GPs vs no disclosure. Clear comparison of PROMs feedback to clinicians vs no feedback on diagnosis and management.
RCT about communication-priming intervention, not about PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals. Different intervention type.
Opinion piece/commentary, not a primary randomised trial.

RCT with 3 arms: (1) patient and rheumatologist see data, (2) only patient sees data, (3) neither sees data. Uses RAPID3 (PROM) for self-assessment. Compares PROMs feedback to clinicians vs no feedback.
Cluster RCT about tailored printouts for cancer risk discussion, not PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals. Different intervention type.
RCT about structured telephone follow-up after surgery, not about PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.
Systematic review, not a primary randomised trial.
Methodological paper about GRADE system, not a primary randomised trial.
Conceptual/review paper about comorbidity definitions, not a primary randomised trial.

RCT comparing SIS.NET (PROMs-based symptom management with NP review) vs standard care. Involves patient-reported outcomes with clinical review. Examines effects on symptom reporting and healthcare resource use.
RCT (FOCUS trial) comparing routine outcome assessment with feedback vs control. Examines PROMs feedback effects on patient outcomes. Clear comparison of PROMs feedback vs no feedback.
RCT comparing HRQoL (PROM) measurement with feedback to physicians (graphical output) vs usual care. Clear comparison of PROMs feedback vs no feedback on outcomes and management.
Overview of phase III trials, not a primary randomised trial comparing PROMs feedback.
Cluster RCT about tailored intervention for guideline implementation, not specifically about PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.
Software description, not a study. Does not meet any criteria.
